tasks.task: Write SQL that answers one business question

items.when: When the question uses a term like active member or net sales that nobody has pinned down
When you write, explain and check a query for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite or SQL Server
When you may run the query on the client's Postgres and it must be read-only
Before the number is shared, to check joins for double counting and rows dropped by mistake
When the owner must confirm in plain words what the query counts and which rows it keeps
When a total looks off, to work it a second way and see if both routes agree

tasks.task: Review and rewrite an existing query

items.when: When nobody remembers what an old query does and you must read it before changing it
Before editing a view, function or table, to list what calls it and what depends on it
When the query gives wrong numbers and needs a readable rewrite with checks
Before a query goes live, to rank wrong-result risks and slow spots with rewrites
When a query is clever but unclear, to work a tiny example by hand and prove each step

tasks.task: Build the queries for a regular report

items.when: When two reports show different numbers for the same thing and one definition must win
When each report line needs its own checked query: sales by month, credits left, reorders
When the report needs retention by sign-up group and you must get the cohort logic right
When the report is a funnel and needs conversion per step and time to convert
When the client wants the numbers pulled into a workbook they can rerun
When a report has run for months and its numbers must be checked against the agreed meaning

tasks.task: Design tables for a new app or feature

items.when: When the business rules are tangled and you need a glossary and which data belongs together
When bookings, memberships, stock or orders must become tables, keys and constraints
When the database is Postgres and column types, indexes and rules need careful choice
When the client is on DynamoDB or Cassandra and tables must follow the queries
When the owner needs a diagram of tables and links they can paste into docs
When a field is added or renamed, to find every place in API and screens that reads it

tasks.task: Turn a busy spreadsheet into proper tables

items.when: Before designing tables, to see the gaps, duplicates and odd values in the sheet today
When part of the business runs on a spreadsheet and needs tables that keep bad data out
When each sheet column needs a written rule for where it goes and how it changes
When the export is messy and must be fixed and re-checked until it loads cleanly
After loading, to match the new tables back to the sheet and list unmatched rows

tasks.task: Plan and run a migration on live tables

items.when: Before a migration runs on live data, to see which statements lock, rewrite or destroy
When any schema or data change will run on production and needs a proven backup first
When the change needs a versioned migration that runs forward and rolls back
When the table has millions of rows and the app must stay up through every step
Before renaming or dropping anything, to find the code and reports that still use it
When the client needs the change written up with impact, risks and who approves
When the plan has no answer for a step that fails halfway, to design the recovery first

tasks.task: Move data from an old layout or tool to a new one

items.when: Before any script, to map each source column to its target with rules and open questions
When data moves between two tools and needs field maps, checks and a way back
When the move is inside one database and needs a versioned script
When both sides are SQL Server and you need schema and row differences listed
After the move, to test for blanks, duplicates and broken links against agreed rules

tasks.task: Write a data dictionary and schema notes

items.when: When nobody fully understands the database and new people need tables, joins and traps
When one important table needs a fuller entry: owner, column meanings and quality notes
When the notes need a diagram of how the main tables link
Before sharing, to find statements that no longer match the real schema

tasks.task: Find why a query is slow and fix it

items.when: When you have the plan output and need to know in plain words why it is slow
When you must pick the worst queries from the logs and rank the fixes for each
When one query is the problem and needs a faster rewrite or an index
When the database is Postgres and settings, types and indexes all need a second look
When tempted to add an index on a hunch, to measure the real path first

tasks.task: Write an index plan from the slow-query log

items.when: When the log shows many slow queries and you need the few indexes worth their write cost
When you want a second ranked list of slow queries, missing indexes and risky schema choices
Before building an index on a busy table, to check it will not block writes

tasks.task: Fix a page that fires hundreds of queries

items.when: When the logs show many near-identical queries per request from ORM code in a loop
When the project is Django and you want every such loop found with its fix
When the client wants the fix in a pull request with before and after timings

tasks.task: Rework a slow endpoint with paging and caching

items.when: When a dashboard or report takes seconds and the bottleneck must be found and proven fixed
When you need a repeatable timing script and a baseline to compare against

tasks.task: Check backups and run a restore drill

items.when: When the owner has never said how much data or time they can afford to lose
When you check how a database is backed up and prove a restore really works
When there are no proper backups and full, incremental and point-in-time ones must be set up
When the drill needs a rehearsal checklist and an evidence record others can read
After a drill, to compare the evidence with the recovery targets and list the gaps
When the client also needs failover and a recovery plan beyond backups

tasks.task: Run the monthly database health check

items.when: Monthly, or after an end-of-life notice, a slow-page complaint or a failed backup alert
During the check, to rank slow queries, missing indexes and risky schema choices
When the check should also score blanks, duplicates and stale rows in key tables
When the last proven restore is older than the client's own rule allows

tasks.task: Write ORM models and seed data for a framework

items.when: Before the models, to settle keys, constraints and delete behaviour
When development and staging need realistic, repeatable rows loaded
When model code must match the framework's current docs, with sources cited

tasks.task: Find bad data and add rules that keep it out

items.when: When you need gaps, duplicates and odd values found, with the rules that would catch them
When the client has rules already and wants each one tested and scored
When the fix is a constraint, a unique key or a foreign key the tables lack
When existing rows must be cleaned before a new rule can be switched on

tasks.task: Plan a move to another database or a newer version

items.when: When the move is Oracle to Postgres and needs scope, baseline tests and a behaviour review
When Oracle procedures must become Postgres code with changed behaviour called out
Before release, to check the migrated code for gaps between the two databases
When the cutover must happen with the app up and a rollback at each step
When cutover day needs its checks, a rollback and a way to know it worked

tasks.task: Choose a database and set-up for a small app

items.when: When the client asks which database to use and wants the options compared
When the choice turns on storage, copies and how consistent the data must be
When the pick must be tested against expected traffic and running cost
When the choice is made, to record why and what was passed over

tasks.task: Set database roles and access rules

items.when: When nobody has written down which kind of user may read or change which data
When the app is on Supabase and must connect with scoped access and safe keys
When AI agents will write to the database and each table needs its own access rule
When an app was built fast with AI and its database rules may be open to anyone

tasks.task: Plan how personal data is kept, found and deleted

items.when: When nobody knows which tables hold personal data and deletion must reach every copy
When the schema must support access, deletion and consent requests and you need the gaps
When a person asks for their data and you need the steps to find it and a draft reply

tasks.task: Diagnose a database outage, lock-up or data loss

items.when: When you have the database log or an error and need the cause found
When the same failure could return and someone needs first steps and who to tell
When it is over and the client needs a blameless report with causes and owners
When rows were lost and a restore to a point in time must be planned

tasks.task: Write or review queries on a data warehouse

items.when: When a warehouse query needs a read-only plan and a check for join and privacy risks
When the warehouse is Snowflake and the SQL must follow its rules
When a BigQuery job costs too much or could double-load on a rerun

always.when: Whenever you write SQL or code for a client's system, to ground it in their real schema
At the end of any job, to write what changed, why and the proof that it works

helpers.when: When the fix is in application code: endpoints, ORM calls, caching or a sync job
When the job is a pipeline or warehouse build, not one database
When the client needs the numbers read and explained, not only the query
When backups, upgrades or failover depend on hosting, servers or a deploy pipeline
When access rules, secrets or injection risks need a full security review
When bad data needs owners, rules and a routine, not a one-off clean

gaps: No library item reads an EXPLAIN plan or the MySQL slow log; only the kit covers query plans
No library item finds N+1 queries outside Django, for example in Rails, Laravel, Prisma or SQLAlchemy
No library item writes ORM models or migrations for Prisma, SQLAlchemy, Django, Laravel or Rails by name
No library item writes a batched backfill script that can stop, resume and be checked by row counts
No library item covers MySQL, SQLite or SQL Server tuning; the tuning items are Postgres only
No library item plans a MySQL to Postgres move, a managed-host move or a major version upgrade
No library item sets database roles, grants or row-level security policies and tests them
No library item diagnoses locks, deadlocks, connection limits, bloat or a full disk
No library item tests a SQL query against a small hand-made dataset with known answers
No library item adds paging and caching to a slow list endpoint
No library item designs audit or history tables, soft deletes or a retention job
